title: Ambient exchange counit, shift compatibility and full-subcategory restriction
statement:
Fix the standing separated finite-type scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] and any commutative condensed ring $R$. Let $p:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, $p':X'\to Y'$ form a commutative square; it need not be cartesian. On ordinary unbounded derived module-object categories write $P_u=Lu^*$, $G_u=Ru_*$ with canonical adjunctions and counits $\varepsilon_u$, and let $\theta:P_{p'}P_g\cong P_{g'}P_p$ be the canonical pullback comparison. Define the ambient map
$$B:P_gG_p\longrightarrow G_{p'}P_{g'}$$
by the unit of $P_{p'}\dashv G_{p'}$, then $G_{p'}\theta$, then $G_{p'}P_{g'}\varepsilon_p$. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X})$, in right-to-left functional notation its components satisfy
$$\varepsilon_{p',P_{g'}K}\circ P_{p'}(B_K)=P_{g'}(\varepsilon_{p,K})\circ\theta_{G_pK}.$$
The two ambient functors are exact and $B$ commutes with their canonical integer-shift comparisons, hence induces morphisms of distinguished triangles including the connecting square. If the four pullbacks and two pushforwards in this formula preserve chosen full triangulated subcategories, and the restricted adjunctions/composition maps are their restrictions, then the restricted $B$ is exactly the unit--square--counit map of [det-def-sfb-base-change-morphism-bc], with the same components. In particular this applies to $\Dbc$ whenever these are full triangulated subcategories and the stated preservation and restriction hypotheses hold.

proof.text: For each arrow $u$, the module-object pullback is exact and additive by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] these are ordinary unbounded total derived functors, computed on K-flat and K-injective resolutions; in particular the ambient module categories have the required resolutions. Apply [def-sfb-left-derived-exact] to identify $P_u$ with the termwise derived pullback $D(u^*)$. The comparison respects the canonical shifts: on a resolution $J\to M$, it is induced by $u^*J\to u^*M$, and on the shifted resolution it is the shift of this map, since exactness sends both resolution arrows to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives the exactness and fixed integer-shift structure of $P_u$. The underived pushforward is additive by [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Apply [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] to it to get the exactness of $G_u$ with its canonical K-injective shift. The two composites $\Phi=P_gG_p$ and $\Psi=G_{p'}P_{g'}$ are exact with composite shift comparisons by [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite].

source.place: Tags 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), 014X (lemma-additive-exact-homotopy-category), 05SE (proposition-derived-functor); exact module pullback from the cited blueprint node

proof.text: The underived adjunction is precisely that of [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction], and its canonical derived adjunction is [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction]. Apply [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift] with $L=u^*$ and $R=u_*$, using the exactness and the resolution hypotheses checked in step 1. It states compatibility with the fixed canonical shifts, so the unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$ commute with every integer shift. This lemma concerns $D(u^*)\dashv G_u$; the specified adjunction is $P_u\dashv G_u$, with $P_u$ computed on K-flat resolutions. Let $c:P_u\cong D(u^*)$ be the canonical isomorphism of step 1. It is the comparison of left derived functors, so $\alpha^D\circ cQ=\alpha^P$ for their comparisons $\alpha^P:P_uQ\to Q\,C(u^*)$ and $\alpha^D:D(u^*)Q\to Q\,C(u^*)$. Both adjunctions are derived adjunctions of $u^*\dashv u_*$ with the same $G_u$ and K-injective comparison $\beta$. By [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived] their counits satisfy $\varepsilon'_{QJ}\circ P'(\beta_J)=Q(\varepsilon_J)\circ\alpha'_{u_*J}$ for $(P',\alpha')=(P_u,\alpha^P),(D(u^*),\alpha^D)$. For K-injective $J$, $\beta_J$ is invertible. Naturality of $c$ then gives $\varepsilon^P_{QJ}=\varepsilon^D_{QJ}\circ c_{G_uQJ}$. Every object is isomorphic to such a $QJ$, so $\varepsilon^P=\varepsilon^D\circ cG_u$. Thus the specified adjunction is the transport of $D(u^*)\dashv G_u$ along $c$, not a newly chosen adjunction on isomorphic functors. Its unit and counit are composites of those of $D(u^*)\dashv G_u$ with $c^{\pm1}$, which is shift-compatible by step 1. They therefore commute with every integer shift.

source.place: Tag 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors); fixed canonical right-derived shift compatibility in the cited general lemma

proof.text: The composition comparison of ambient pullbacks is the one induced by the underived comparison, by [prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp]. To check its shifts, use the exact termwise descriptions from step 1. Write $b:(vu)^*\cong u^*v^*$ for the underived comparison. By [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso] and [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition], its derived comparison is represented on every complex $M$ by the degreewise map $b_{M^r}$ followed by the termwise composition identification. For $M[n]$ the degree-$r$ component is $b_{M^{r+n}}$, exactly the degree-$r$ component of the shifted comparison; both differentials are multiplied by $(-1)^n$. The localization factorizations in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] respect these shifts. Every derived object is represented by a complex, so this proves the shift square for the canonical composition comparison for all $n\in\mathbf Z$. The same equation for its inverse follows by multiplying the square by inverse isomorphisms. The comparison $\theta$ is the inverse compositor for $(p',g)$ followed by the compositor for $(g',p)$, with the equality $gp'=pg'$ in between. The equality inserts identical termwise functors, hence respects shifts. Therefore $\theta$ commutes with all integer shifts.

proof.text:
Fix $K$. Put $A=P_gG_pK$, $C=P_{g'}K$, $F=P_{p'}$, $H=G_{p'}$, and $a=P_{g'}(\varepsilon_{p,K})\circ\theta_{G_pK}:FA\to C$. The definition gives $B_K=H(a)\circ\eta'_{A}$. Naturality of the counit of $F\dashv H$ gives $\varepsilon'_{C}\circ FH(a)=a\circ\varepsilon'_{FA}$. Consequently
$$\varepsilon'_C\circ F(B_K)=a\circ\varepsilon'_{FA}\circ F(\eta'_A)=a,$$
where the last equality is the adjunction triangle identity. This is exactly the asserted counit equation. Only the adjunction laws of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] are used; cartesianness plays no role.

proof.text:
Let $\chi_\Phi^n(K):\Phi(K[n])\to\Phi(K)[n]$ and $\chi_\Psi^n(K):\Psi(K[n])\to\Psi(K)[n]$ be the composite comparisons. The three transformations making up $B$ are the unit for $p'$ whiskered by $P_gG_p$, the comparison $\theta$ whiskered by $G_{p'}$ and $G_p$, and the counit for $p$ whiskered by $G_{p'}P_{g'}$. Steps 2 and 3 make each factor shift-compatible. Apply the composition and whiskering rules of [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker], for each shift $[n]$, to obtain
$$\chi_\Psi^n(K)\circ B_{K[n]}=B_K[n]\circ\chi_\Phi^n(K).$$
Here $B$ is a natural transformation because it is a composite of whiskered natural transformations.

source.place: paragraph (3): the canonical exchange is a natural transformation of exact functors; fixed shifts checked in steps 2--3

proof.text:
For a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow{u}L\xrightarrow{v}M\xrightarrow{w}K[1]$, the image triangles under $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are distinguished by step 1. Naturality of $B$ gives the squares for $u$ and $v$. For the last square, naturality at $w$ and step 5 give
$$\chi_\Psi^1(K)\circ\Psi(w)\circ B_M
=\chi_\Psi^1(K)\circ B_{K[1]}\circ\Phi(w)
=B_K[1]\circ\chi_\Phi^1(K)\circ\Phi(w).$$
Thus $(B_K,B_L,B_M)$ is a morphism of the two image triangles, including their connecting arrows, by the definition of a triangle morphism in [def-weil-triangulated-category].

source.place: paragraph (3): connecting square required for triangle devissage

proof.text: Now impose exactly the stated preservation and restriction hypotheses. Every object occurring in the three factors of $B_K$ then belongs to its chosen subcategory. A full-subcategory inclusion leaves Hom sets, identities and composition unchanged, so the same three arrows define the restricted natural transformation. By the assumed restriction of the adjunctions and composition maps, these arrows are respectively the restricted unit, $G_{p'}$ of the restricted square comparison, and $G_{p'}P_{g'}$ of the restricted counit. Their composite is word for word the formula of [det-def-sfb-base-change-morphism-bc], with $f=p$ and $f'=p'$. Fullness and faithfulness make equality of the ambient components equality of the restricted components. Shifts and distinguished triangles are inherited by [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], so steps 4--6 remain valid. For $\Dbc$ its morphisms are explicitly the ambient morphisms by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]; the conclusion applies whenever the preservation hypotheses in the statement hold.
